quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A team of agricultural researchers comparing crop yields across a large number of farms noted that farms using a particular soil amendment reported yields twelve percent higher on average than farms not using it, a pattern that held consistently across farms in five different climate zones and three different soil types, though the researchers cautioned that farms choosing to purchase the amendment may also differ in other unmeasured ways, such as overall investment in soil health practices, that could partly explain the yield difference.
options: The soil amendment's association with higher yields may be partly explained by other farming practices the researchers did not measure.
The soil amendment is proven to be the sole cause of the twelve percent yield increase.
Farms using the amendment reported yields lower than farms that did not use it.
The yield pattern held only in a single climate zone and soil type.
quests.correctAnswer: The soil amendment's association with higher yields may be partly explained by other farming practices the researchers did not measure.
quests.hint: Notice the researchers' own caution near the end of the passage about what else might explain the pattern.
quests.explanation: The yield difference held across many climate zones and soil types, but the researchers themselves noted that farms using the amendment might also invest more broadly in soil health, meaning the amendment's true individual effect remains uncertain rather than proven.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A workplace analytics firm reviewing performance data from several dozen client companies found that teams whose members had overlapping working hours of at least four hours per day, even when working from different locations, completed collaborative projects faster on average than teams with less overlap, but the firm noted this pattern was strongest specifically for projects requiring frequent back-and-forth revision, such as design work, and much weaker for projects that were primarily completed independently before a final review.
options: Overlapping hours mattered equally for every type of project studied.
Projects completed independently benefited the most from overlapping hours.
Overlapping work hours appear to matter most for collaborative work requiring frequent revision, rather than for all project types equally.
The amount of overlap in working hours had no bearing on project completion speed.
quests.correctAnswer: Overlapping work hours appear to matter most for collaborative work requiring frequent revision, rather than for all project types equally.
quests.hint: Notice the passage specifies which type of project showed the strongest pattern.
quests.explanation: The benefit of overlapping hours was strongest for projects needing frequent revision and weaker for independent work, suggesting the advantage comes specifically from enabling real-time back-and-forth collaboration rather than simply being a general boost to all teamwork.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A district evaluating a new algebra curriculum piloted it in ten randomly selected classrooms while ten similar classrooms continued using the previous curriculum, allowing for a reasonably controlled comparison. Students in the pilot classrooms scored higher on a common end-of-year assessment, but the difference was concentrated almost entirely among students who had scored in the middle range on a placement test at the start of the year, with little measurable difference among students who had scored in the highest or lowest ranges.
options: The new curriculum benefited students equally across every ability range.
The new curriculum appears to have specifically benefited students who started in the middle range of ability.
The new curriculum benefited only the highest-scoring students.
The curriculum had no measurable effect on any group of students.
quests.correctAnswer: The new curriculum appears to have specifically benefited students who started in the middle range of ability.
quests.hint: Notice which specific group of students showed the largest difference in scores.
quests.explanation: The pilot curriculum's benefit was concentrated among middle-range students, with little difference for the highest or lowest scorers, suggesting the new approach was particularly well suited to students who weren't already excelling or significantly struggling.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A public health researcher comparing counties with different approaches to reducing opioid-related emergency room visits found that counties combining expanded access to a specific overdose-reversal medication with mobile outreach teams that could distribute it directly to at-risk individuals saw a much larger reduction in overdose deaths than counties that expanded access to the medication through pharmacies alone, without any accompanying direct outreach component, according to state health department data collected over a three-year period.
options: Pharmacy access alone was more effective than combining it with outreach teams.
Direct outreach appears to add meaningful benefit beyond simply expanding pharmacy access to the medication alone.
Neither approach had any measurable effect on overdose deaths.
Outreach teams were effective only when pharmacy access was simultaneously reduced.
quests.correctAnswer: Direct outreach appears to add meaningful benefit beyond simply expanding pharmacy access to the medication alone.
quests.hint: Compare counties that combined both approaches with counties that used only one.
quests.explanation: Counties combining medication access with direct outreach saw larger reductions in overdose deaths than counties relying on pharmacy access alone, suggesting that reaching at-risk individuals directly added a benefit beyond simply making the medication available somewhere in the community.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A tourism research group studying traveler behavior across several major cities found that cities which invested heavily in multilingual signage throughout public transit systems saw increases in the average length of stay reported by international visitors, but cities that invested similarly in multilingual signage without also training frontline transit staff in basic conversational phrases saw a notably smaller increase, suggesting signage alone may not fully address the communication barriers visitors experience while actually navigating an unfamiliar system in real time.
options: Multilingual signage combined with staff training appears more effective than signage alone at improving visitors' experience.
Signage alone was more effective than combining it with staff training.
Staff training had no measurable effect on visitor length of stay.
Multilingual signage had no effect on visitor behavior in any city studied.
quests.correctAnswer: Multilingual signage combined with staff training appears more effective than signage alone at improving visitors' experience.
quests.hint: Compare cities that combined signage with staff training to cities that relied on signage alone.
quests.explanation: Cities pairing signage with staff training saw larger increases in visitor stays than cities using signage alone, suggesting that human interaction, not just written information, plays an important role in addressing the communication challenges travelers face.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A team evaluating an AI-assisted diagnostic tool for radiologists found that diagnostic accuracy improved when radiologists used the tool as a 'second opinion' after forming their own initial assessment, but accuracy showed no improvement, and in a few cases slightly worsened, when radiologists were shown the AI's suggestion before forming their own independent judgment, a pattern the researchers attributed to a tendency to defer to the tool's suggestion too readily when it was presented first.
options: Seeing the AI's suggestion first always improved diagnostic accuracy the most.
The order of information had no bearing on diagnostic accuracy.
The order in which a radiologist encounters the AI's suggestion, relative to their own judgment, appears to affect how helpful the tool is.
Diagnostic accuracy declined regardless of when the AI's suggestion was shown.
quests.correctAnswer: The order in which a radiologist encounters the AI's suggestion, relative to their own judgment, appears to affect how helpful the tool is.
quests.hint: Compare the two different orders in which radiologists could encounter the AI's suggestion.
quests.explanation: Accuracy improved when the AI was used as a second opinion after an initial judgment, but not when shown first, suggesting radiologists may have deferred too readily to the AI's suggestion when it came before their own independent assessment.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: An economist analyzing consumer spending patterns during a period of high inflation found that households which had built an emergency savings fund equivalent to at least three months of expenses before the inflationary period began reduced their discretionary spending by a smaller percentage than households without such a fund, even though both groups experienced comparable increases in their essential monthly costs, such as groceries, fuel, and utilities, over the same twelve-month period the economist analyzed.
options: Households with emergency savings cut discretionary spending more sharply than those without.
Essential costs rose only for households without emergency savings.
Emergency savings had no bearing on how households responded to rising costs.
Having pre-existing emergency savings appears to have cushioned households from cutting discretionary spending as sharply during inflation.
quests.correctAnswer: Having pre-existing emergency savings appears to have cushioned households from cutting discretionary spending as sharply during inflation.
quests.hint: Compare spending changes between the two groups, noting that essential costs rose similarly for both.
quests.explanation: Households with pre-existing emergency savings cut discretionary spending less than households without savings, even with similar increases in essential costs, suggesting the savings buffer allowed them to absorb rising costs without cutting back as much elsewhere.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A longitudinal study following young adults who grew up with divorced parents found that those whose parents maintained a low-conflict co-parenting relationship after separation, communicating primarily about logistics rather than airing personal grievances in front of the children, reported similar levels of relationship satisfaction in their own adult romantic relationships as young adults raised by married parents, while young adults whose parents maintained a high-conflict co-parenting relationship reported notably lower relationship satisfaction than either of the other two groups studied.
options: Divorce itself, regardless of co-parenting conflict, was the main factor in later relationship satisfaction.
The level of conflict between co-parents, rather than divorce itself, appears more closely linked to children's later relationship satisfaction.
Low-conflict co-parenting led to worse outcomes than high-conflict co-parenting.
All three groups reported identical relationship satisfaction as adults.
quests.correctAnswer: The level of conflict between co-parents, rather than divorce itself, appears more closely linked to children's later relationship satisfaction.
quests.hint: Compare outcomes across all three groups, noting which factor seems to distinguish them.
quests.explanation: Children of low-conflict divorced parents fared similarly to children of married parents, while children of high-conflict divorced parents fared worse, suggesting that ongoing conflict, rather than divorce itself, is more closely tied to later relationship satisfaction.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: Researchers comparing carbon capture efficiency of urban tree species found that species with denser canopy coverage captured measurably more airborne particulate pollution per tree, but a full cost-benefit analysis that included water usage requirements, root damage to nearby sidewalks and pipes, and long-term maintenance costs found that a mid-density species performed better overall as a citywide street tree recommendation than the single highest-density species when city planning budgets and infrastructure costs were factored into the final recommendation.
options: The best tree species for pollution capture alone was not necessarily the best overall choice once other costs were considered.
The highest-density species was recommended based on pollution capture alone, without further analysis.
Water usage and root damage were not considered relevant factors in the analysis.
All tree species performed identically once maintenance costs were included.
quests.correctAnswer: The best tree species for pollution capture alone was not necessarily the best overall choice once other costs were considered.
quests.hint: Notice the passage distinguishes between pollution capture alone and the full cost-benefit analysis.
quests.explanation: The highest-density species captured the most pollution, but a mid-density species was recommended overall once water use, infrastructure damage, and maintenance were factored in, showing that the single best-performing option on one measure wasn't necessarily the best overall choice.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A municipal government piloting participatory budgeting, in which residents directly vote on how to allocate a small portion of the city budget, found that neighborhoods with historically low voter turnout in general elections showed disproportionately high participation in the budgeting votes specifically, a pattern city officials attributed to the tangible, local nature of the decisions being voted on, compared to the often more abstract and distant stakes of a typical municipal election, according to participation data compiled after the pilot's first year.
options: Participatory budgeting attracted mainly residents who already voted frequently in general elections.
Participatory budgeting appears to have specifically engaged residents who typically don't vote in general elections.
Neighborhoods with low general election turnout also showed low turnout in the budgeting votes.
The type of decision being voted on had no bearing on participation rates.
quests.correctAnswer: Participatory budgeting appears to have specifically engaged residents who typically don't vote in general elections.
quests.hint: Notice which specific neighborhoods showed the biggest jump in participation.
quests.explanation: Neighborhoods with historically low voter turnout showed unusually high participation in the budgeting votes specifically, suggesting the tangible, local nature of participatory budgeting engaged residents who don't typically turn out for more abstract general elections.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A national gymnastics federation reviewing several seasons of injury data across its youth programs found that gyms requiring a mandatory rest week between competition seasons reported significantly fewer overuse injuries, such as stress fractures, than gyms that allowed athletes to train through the transition without any scheduled break, though the federation noted that gyms with mandatory rest weeks also tended to have, on average, more experienced head coaches than gyms without the requirement in place.
options: The rest week is proven to be the only factor explaining the lower injury rate.
Gyms without mandatory rest weeks reported fewer overuse injuries.
The lower injury rate at rest-week gyms may be partly explained by coaching experience rather than the rest week alone.
Coaching experience was unrelated to whether a gym required a rest week.
quests.correctAnswer: The lower injury rate at rest-week gyms may be partly explained by coaching experience rather than the rest week alone.
quests.hint: Notice the federation's own observation about a difference between the two types of gyms besides the rest week itself.
quests.explanation: Gyms with mandatory rest weeks had fewer injuries, but they also tended to have more experienced coaches, meaning the rest week's true individual contribution to injury reduction is uncertain, since coaching experience could also be playing a role.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A museum studying visitor engagement with its permanent collection found that adding short audio commentary, narrated by the artist or a close family member when available rather than a professional narrator, kept visitors at a given artwork for measurably longer, and post-visit surveys showed higher recall of specific artwork details among visitors who had listened to the personal commentary compared to visitors who saw the same artwork without any audio commentary at all.
options: Personal commentary reduced how long visitors spent with each artwork.
Visitors who heard no commentary recalled more artwork details.
The source of the audio commentary had no bearing on visitor engagement or recall.
Personal commentary from someone connected to the artwork appears to improve both engagement and memory of the details.
quests.correctAnswer: Personal commentary from someone connected to the artwork appears to improve both engagement and memory of the details.
quests.hint: Notice the passage mentions two separate positive outcomes linked to the personal commentary.
quests.explanation: Visitors spent more time and recalled more details when personal commentary was available, suggesting a personal, connected voice engaged visitors more deeply than generic narration, affecting both how long they looked and what they remembered afterward.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A manufacturing firm comparing safety outcomes across its facilities found that facilities where floor supervisors were required to personally demonstrate a safety procedure to new hires, rather than simply reviewing a written checklist together, reported fewer safety incidents among employees in their first ninety days, even though both training methods covered the exact same procedures and took approximately the same amount of time to complete, according to incident reports compiled across all facilities over two years.
options: Hands-on demonstration during training appears more effective at preventing early safety incidents than a written review alone, despite similar time and content.
Written checklist review was more effective than hands-on demonstration.
The training method had no bearing on safety incidents among new hires.
The two training methods covered different procedures and took different amounts of time.
quests.correctAnswer: Hands-on demonstration during training appears more effective at preventing early safety incidents than a written review alone, despite similar time and content.
quests.hint: Notice what stayed the same between the two training methods, and what differed.
quests.explanation: Facilities using hands-on demonstration had fewer early safety incidents than those using written checklists alone, even with identical content and time, suggesting the format of training itself, not just its content, affects how well new hires retain safety procedures.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A food industry analyst tracking sales of a popular snack brand across different regions found that a reformulation reducing sodium content by twenty percent led to a modest sales decline in regions where the change was prominently advertised on packaging as a health improvement, but sales in regions where the identical reformulated product was sold with no mention of the sodium change on the packaging remained essentially flat compared to sales of the previous formulation one year earlier.
options: The reformulation itself, regardless of advertising, caused sales to decline everywhere.
Advertising the health-focused reformulation appears to have hurt sales more than the reformulation itself.
Sales increased in regions where the change was prominently advertised.
Advertising the change had no bearing on sales in either region.
quests.correctAnswer: Advertising the health-focused reformulation appears to have hurt sales more than the reformulation itself.
quests.hint: Compare sales in regions where the change was advertised to regions where it wasn't mentioned.
quests.explanation: Sales declined only where the sodium reduction was advertised as a health change, while sales stayed flat where the identical product change went unmentioned, suggesting customers reacted negatively to the framing of the change rather than to the product itself.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A team studying urban heat islands across several metropolitan regions found that painting rooftops white to reflect sunlight reduced indoor cooling costs measurably during summer months, but researchers also observed that the cooling benefit was substantially smaller in cities with high humidity compared to cities with similar summer temperatures but noticeably lower humidity, a finding the research team noted has real implications for which cities should prioritize the technique within their broader heat-mitigation strategies.
options: White rooftops appear less effective at reducing cooling costs in humid climates than in drier ones with similar temperatures.
White rooftops were equally effective regardless of a city's humidity level.
White rooftops were more effective in humid cities than in dry ones.
Humidity had no measurable relationship to the cooling benefit of white rooftops.
quests.correctAnswer: White rooftops appear less effective at reducing cooling costs in humid climates than in drier ones with similar temperatures.
quests.hint: Compare the cooling benefit between humid and low-humidity cities with similar temperatures.
quests.explanation: The cooling benefit of white rooftops was smaller in humid cities than in drier cities with similar temperatures, suggesting that humidity affects how well this particular technique works, beyond temperature alone.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A team studying electric vehicle charging behavior found that drivers with home charging access, allowing them to charge overnight, expressed significantly less anxiety about running out of charge during daily errands than drivers who relied entirely on public charging stations, even though public charging infrastructure in the drivers' city had expanded considerably in the two years leading up to the survey, according to responses from several hundred electric vehicle owners across the metropolitan area.
options: Public charging expansion eliminated range anxiety for all drivers.
Drivers relying on public charging reported less anxiety than those with home access.
Access to home charging had no bearing on drivers' anxiety levels.
Home charging access appears to reduce range anxiety more than simply having more public charging stations available.
quests.correctAnswer: Home charging access appears to reduce range anxiety more than simply having more public charging stations available.
quests.hint: Notice that public charging had expanded, yet a difference in anxiety still remained between the two groups.
quests.explanation: Drivers with home charging reported less anxiety than those relying on public stations, even after public infrastructure expanded, suggesting the convenience and predictability of home charging addresses anxiety in a way that public station availability alone does not.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A clinical team studying medication adherence among patients with chronic conditions found that patients who received a brief phone call from a pharmacist within forty-eight hours of starting a new prescription were significantly more likely to still be taking the medication correctly at the three-month mark than patients who received only the standard printed instructions, with the effect being most pronounced among patients managing more than one chronic condition simultaneously, a group pharmacists noted often faces the most complex schedules.
options: The pharmacist call was equally effective regardless of how many conditions a patient managed.
Patients managing multiple conditions benefited least from the pharmacist call.
Printed instructions alone were more effective than a pharmacist's follow-up call.
The early pharmacist call appears especially valuable for patients managing multiple chronic conditions at once.
quests.correctAnswer: The early pharmacist call appears especially valuable for patients managing multiple chronic conditions at once.
quests.hint: Notice which specific group of patients showed the strongest effect from the pharmacist's call.
quests.explanation: The pharmacist call's benefit was strongest among patients managing multiple chronic conditions, suggesting that patients facing the most complex medication schedules gained the most from that early, personal follow-up.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A regional tourism board comparing visitor spending patterns found that tourists who booked at least one guided local experience, such as a cooking class or walking tour, in advance of their trip spent notably more at independent local businesses throughout their entire stay than tourists who arrived without any pre-booked activities, even after controlling for differences in overall trip length and total travel budget between the two groups of travelers surveyed.
options: Trip length and budget fully explained the difference in local spending.
Tourists without pre-booked activities spent more at local businesses overall.
Pre-booking a local experience had no bearing on overall spending patterns.
Booking a local experience in advance appears linked to greater overall local spending, beyond what trip length or budget alone would explain.
quests.correctAnswer: Booking a local experience in advance appears linked to greater overall local spending, beyond what trip length or budget alone would explain.
quests.hint: Notice the passage mentions that trip length and budget were accounted for separately from the spending pattern.
quests.explanation: Tourists who pre-booked a local experience spent more at local businesses overall, even after accounting for trip length and budget, suggesting that an early local connection may encourage more local spending throughout an entire visit.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A university department reviewing several years of course evaluation data found that instructors who posted detailed lecture slides online before class, allowing students to preview material in advance, received similar overall satisfaction ratings to instructors who did not post materials in advance, but received notably higher ratings specifically on questions related to how well the course accommodated different learning styles and paces, a distinction that stood out clearly across the aggregated responses the department reviewed.
options: Posting materials in advance improved every category of course evaluation equally.
Instructors who posted materials in advance received lower overall satisfaction ratings.
Posting materials in advance had no measurable effect on any evaluation category.
Posting materials in advance appears to specifically improve perceived accommodation of different learning styles, without changing overall satisfaction much.
quests.correctAnswer: Posting materials in advance appears to specifically improve perceived accommodation of different learning styles, without changing overall satisfaction much.
quests.hint: Notice the passage separates overall satisfaction from one specific category of evaluation.
quests.explanation: Overall satisfaction stayed similar regardless of whether materials were posted in advance, but ratings on accommodating different learning styles rose specifically, suggesting the advance materials helped students with different needs more than they changed general course satisfaction.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A recycling facility that switched from single-stream sorting, where all recyclables are mixed together in one bin and separated later by machine, to a dual-stream system requiring residents to separate paper from other materials at home, found that overall recycling volume dropped in the months just after the switch, but the contamination rate, the percentage of non-recyclable material mixed in, fell so significantly that the total amount of usable recycled material actually increased despite the lower total volume collected.
options: The dual-stream system reduced both total volume and usable recycled material.
Contamination rates increased under the dual-stream system.
The dual-stream system appears to have improved the usable quality of recycling more than the drop in total volume hurt it.
Total volume and contamination rates were unaffected by the switch to dual-stream sorting.
quests.correctAnswer: The dual-stream system appears to have improved the usable quality of recycling more than the drop in total volume hurt it.
quests.hint: Notice the passage distinguishes between total volume collected and the amount of usable material within that volume.
quests.explanation: Total recycling volume dropped, but contamination fell enough that usable recycled material actually increased, suggesting that quality, not just quantity, matters for how much recycling ultimately gets put to good use.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: An analysis of small business loan defaults found that businesses that had completed a free consultation with a local Small Business Development Center before applying for financing defaulted at lower rates than businesses that had not, but the effect was concentrated almost entirely among first-time business owners, with little measurable difference in default rates among owners who had previously run at least one other business before their current venture, according to data reviewed across several regional lenders.
options: The consultation benefited experienced business owners more than first-time owners.
The consultation had an identical effect regardless of the owner's prior experience.
The consultation appears to specifically benefit first-time business owners more than experienced ones.
Default rates were unaffected by whether a business owner attended a consultation.
quests.correctAnswer: The consultation appears to specifically benefit first-time business owners more than experienced ones.
quests.hint: Notice which specific group of business owners showed the largest difference in default rates.
quests.explanation: The consultation's benefit was concentrated among first-time owners, with little effect for experienced owners, suggesting the guidance addressed gaps in knowledge that experienced owners had likely already filled through prior experience running a business.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A family mediator who works with co-parenting families going through custody arrangements observed that families using a shared digital calendar to coordinate schedules and expenses reported fewer disputes requiring formal mediation over an eighteen-month period than families relying on informal text messages and phone calls, though the mediator noted this pattern held most strongly for families who had already agreed on a basic custody framework before adopting the digital calendar as their primary coordination tool.
options: The digital calendar was equally helpful regardless of whether a custody framework existed.
Families using text messages and calls had fewer disputes than those using a calendar.
A shared digital calendar appears most helpful for families who already have a basic custody agreement in place.
The mediator found no relationship between coordination method and dispute frequency.
quests.correctAnswer: A shared digital calendar appears most helpful for families who already have a basic custody agreement in place.
quests.hint: Notice the condition the mediator mentions under which the pattern held most strongly.
quests.explanation: The digital calendar was linked to fewer disputes, but this pattern was strongest for families with an existing custody framework, suggesting the tool works best at reducing logistical friction once the bigger disagreements have already been resolved.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A city analyzing participation in its free tax preparation assistance program, aimed at low- and moderate-income residents, found that participation rates were significantly higher in neighborhoods where the program was promoted through partnerships with local churches, community centers, and small businesses that residents already knew and regularly visited, than in neighborhoods where promotion relied primarily on the city's official website and printed mailers sent to every eligible household, according to enrollment data compiled at the conclusion of that tax season.
options: Promotion through trusted local community institutions appears more effective than official city communications for reaching eligible residents.
Official city communications were more effective than community partnerships.
The method of promotion had no bearing on program participation rates.
Participation rates were identical regardless of how the program was promoted.
quests.correctAnswer: Promotion through trusted local community institutions appears more effective than official city communications for reaching eligible residents.
quests.hint: Compare participation in neighborhoods that used different promotion strategies.
quests.explanation: Participation was higher in neighborhoods where trusted local institutions promoted the program than where the city relied on official channels alone, suggesting that community trust and familiarity may matter more than the source alone for reaching residents effectively.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A college athletic department comparing recovery outcomes for athletes with similar knee injuries found that athletes who began supervised physical therapy within one week of injury, rather than waiting the more traditional two to three weeks to allow initial swelling to fully subside, returned to competition faster on average, with no measurable increase in re-injury rates during their first full season back, based on outcomes tracked by the department's sports medicine staff over several seasons.
options: Starting physical therapy earlier appears to speed recovery without increasing the risk of re-injury.
Starting therapy earlier increased the rate of re-injury significantly.
Waiting two to three weeks led to faster return times.
The timing of physical therapy had no bearing on recovery speed or re-injury rates.
quests.correctAnswer: Starting physical therapy earlier appears to speed recovery without increasing the risk of re-injury.
quests.hint: Notice the passage mentions two separate outcomes: return speed and re-injury rate.
quests.explanation: Athletes who started therapy earlier returned to competition faster, and re-injury rates stayed similar, suggesting the traditional waiting period may not have been necessary to protect against further injury.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A public radio station that shifted a portion of its funding appeals from lengthy, multi-day on-air pledge drives to shorter, more frequent reminders embedded naturally within regular programming found that total annual donations remained roughly the same as in previous years, but listener complaints about programming interruptions dropped substantially, and average listening time per session increased slightly during the months following the change, according to internal ratings data reviewed at fiscal year's end.
options: Donations declined significantly after the funding appeal format changed.
Listener complaints increased after the format change.
The shorter, more frequent appeals appear to have maintained donations while improving the listener experience.
The format of funding appeals had no measurable effect on donations or listener experience.
quests.correctAnswer: The shorter, more frequent appeals appear to have maintained donations while improving the listener experience.
quests.hint: Notice the passage mentions one outcome that stayed the same and two that improved.
quests.explanation: Donations held steady while complaints dropped and listening time rose slightly, suggesting the shorter, embedded appeals achieved the same fundraising result while creating a noticeably better experience for listeners.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A staffing analytics firm studying multi-year attrition among call center employees found that employees hired through an internal employee-referral program, where current staff recommend candidates from their own personal networks, stayed in their positions substantially longer on average than employees hired through traditional external job postings, even after the firm statistically controlled for starting pay, shift assignment, prior call center experience, and initial training scores across both groups of newly hired employees.
options: Being hired through employee referral appears linked to longer tenure, beyond what pay, shift, or experience alone would explain.
Pay and shift assignment fully explained the difference in employee tenure.
Employees hired through external postings stayed longer on average.
How an employee was hired had no bearing on how long they stayed.
quests.correctAnswer: Being hired through employee referral appears linked to longer tenure, beyond what pay, shift, or experience alone would explain.
quests.hint: Notice the passage lists several factors the firm accounted for separately from the hiring method itself.
quests.explanation: Referred employees stayed longer even after accounting for pay, shift, and experience, suggesting the referral process itself, perhaps through better-set expectations or an existing personal connection, contributed to longer tenure beyond those other measured factors.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A team studying software developer productivity found that developers working in a codebase with comprehensive automated tests wrote new features faster on average than developers working in a similar codebase with minimal test coverage, but the productivity gap widened considerably as the codebase's overall size and complexity increased, suggesting the value of automated testing may become more pronounced as software projects grow larger and harder to reason about over time.
options: The productivity gap remained constant regardless of codebase size.
Automated testing appears to provide a growing advantage as codebases become larger and more complex, not just a fixed benefit.
Automated testing provided the biggest advantage in the smallest codebases.
Codebase size and complexity had no bearing on the benefit of automated testing.
quests.correctAnswer: Automated testing appears to provide a growing advantage as codebases become larger and more complex, not just a fixed benefit.
quests.hint: Notice how the productivity gap changed as codebase size and complexity increased.
quests.explanation: The productivity advantage of automated testing widened as codebases grew larger and more complex, suggesting the benefit isn't fixed but instead compounds as a software project becomes bigger and harder to manage without reliable tests.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: Researchers studying urban bird populations found that cities that reduced nighttime lighting in downtown areas during peak spring and fall migration periods, when many bird species travel at night guided partly by natural light cues, recorded substantially fewer bird deaths from building collisions than cities that maintained normal lighting levels year-round, even though the participating cities were otherwise similar in building density and overall population size, according to collision data collected across multiple migration seasons.
options: Reduced nighttime lighting increased bird collision deaths during migration.
Reducing nighttime lighting during migration season appears to reduce bird collision deaths, independent of a city's size or density.
Building density was the main factor explaining collision death rates.
Lighting levels had no bearing on bird collision deaths in any city studied.
quests.correctAnswer: Reducing nighttime lighting during migration season appears to reduce bird collision deaths, independent of a city's size or density.
quests.hint: Notice that building density and size were similar between the compared cities.
quests.explanation: Cities that dimmed lights during migration season had fewer bird collision deaths than similarly sized cities with normal lighting, suggesting the lighting change itself, not other city characteristics, was linked to the improvement.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A restaurant consultant analyzing menu design across dozens of client restaurants over several years found that menus listing prices without a dollar sign, showing simply '24' instead of '$24,' were associated with slightly higher average spending per table than menus using the traditional dollar sign format, a pattern the consultant attributed to the dollar sign serving as a subtle visual reminder of the act of spending money, based on informal diner interviews conducted at several of the restaurants studied.
options: Including the dollar sign was associated with higher average spending.
The presence or absence of a dollar sign had no bearing on spending.
Average spending per table was identical regardless of menu price format.
Removing the dollar sign from menu prices appears associated with higher average spending.
quests.correctAnswer: Removing the dollar sign from menu prices appears associated with higher average spending.
quests.hint: Compare average spending between the two menu price formats.
quests.explanation: Menus without a dollar sign were linked to slightly higher spending than menus with one, suggesting that a small visual detail, the presence of a currency symbol, may subtly influence how much diners spend.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: Since the Hendersons began keeping a small whiteboard in their kitchen listing each family member's activities and any needed items for the week, they say they have reduced last-minute store runs considerably compared to the previous year, though they also noted the system only works reliably when someone actually updates the board consistently, since it fell into disuse for several weeks last spring during a particularly busy stretch and old habits of forgetting items briefly returned.
options: The whiteboard system worked well even during the weeks it was neglected.
The whiteboard system appears effective at reducing last-minute errands, but only when family members keep it consistently updated.
Last-minute store runs increased after the family started using the whiteboard.
The whiteboard had no measurable effect on the family's errands regardless of use.
quests.correctAnswer: The whiteboard system appears effective at reducing last-minute errands, but only when family members keep it consistently updated.
quests.hint: Notice what happened when the family temporarily stopped updating the board.
quests.explanation: The system reduced last-minute errands overall, but old habits returned during the weeks it went unused, showing that the whiteboard's benefit depends on consistent upkeep rather than being effective automatically just by existing in the kitchen.
